content.text:
I submitted **index 4 (Bi 0.40, Cu 0.19, V 0.41)**, the best of the three compositions I measured, at **8.28 µA** photocurrent. With only three measurements across 143 candidates, I can't tell whether it's the best in the library.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent | Why I picked it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 | **8.28 µA** | Close to a 1:1 Bi:V ratio (like BiVO₄, a well-known photoanode), and among the lowest Cu in the library |
| 44 | 0.09 / 0.52 / 0.39 | 3.17 µA | The Cu-vanadate area, the other plausible photoanode family |
| 7 | 0.43 / 0.18 / 0.39 | 0.98 µA | Next to index 4, with the least Cu in the library |

- **Region:** the Bi:V ≈ 1:1 area beat the Cu-vanadate area.
- **Sharp drop:** index 7 differs only slightly from index 4 but gave about an eighth of the photocurrent. So small composition changes matter here, and untested points near index 4 (such as 62, 104 or 3) could be better or worse.
- **Unused tools:** I spent none of the 5 XRD measurements and didn't use the GP suggestion tool. I have no data on which crystal phases are present, so the link to BiVO₄ is based on composition only.
